comments.author: Joffcom
comments.text:
@rmyndharis this would be a bit worrying as it would suggest all trigger nodes that use static data have been broken for months but I have not seen any reports of that which is interesting.

Can you share more information on what you were doing when you found this as it may help provide a bit more context as to why this isn't a bigger issue.

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: I checked the current `master` source at `packages/cli/src/workflow-runner.ts`: `establishContextForPersistence()` constructs `contextWorkflow` with `staticData: data.workflowData.staticData` (around line 387), despite the adjacent comment saying this lightweight workflow uses “no staticData loading.” That confirms the object is still passed into this context workflow; I have not independently verified the `Workflow`/`ObservableObject` mutation behavior or run your reproduction. A focused regression test or PR demonstrating the reported `2.19.0` vs `2.19.2` behavior would help maintainers validate the proposed fix.

comments.author: rmyndharis
comments.text:
Thanks for taking a look, @Joffcom. I agree it would be surprising if this hit many nodes. As far as I can tell it hits very few, for the reasons below.

**How I found it.** I maintain a community node for a WhatsApp gateway. Its webhook trigger de-duplicates retried deliveries by keeping a ring of seen keys in node static data, written from `webhook()`. While checking the node against several n8n versions, the ring stopped persisting from 2.19.2. The trigger node in the issue reproduces the same loss without my node.

**Why it is probably not visible elsewhere.** The loss only affects static data written from inside `webhook()` on a production run. The usual use of static data in webhook triggers is the remote webhook ID written in `webhookMethods.create`, which is saved on a different path and still works (the repro stores a `remoteId` there and it persists).

I checked the built-in nodes. Ten `webhook()` implementations touch static data: Bitbucket, Cisco Webex, ClickUp, HelpScout, Jira, Mailchimp, PayPal, Strava, WooCommerce and Wufoo. Nine only read what activation stored. The one that writes per delivery is the Jira Trigger with OAuth2, which stores `lastRefreshed`. If that write is lost, the node refreshes the webhook again on the next delivery, so nothing looks wrong. I have not looked at polling triggers.

The numbers from the repro are in the issue (1.123.87 and 2.19.0 give 1, 2, 3; 2.19.2 and 2.45.3 give 1, 1, 1). #42081 has the one-line change and a regression test that fails on `master` and passes with it.
